## Horizontal alternating-sequence gap fill (observed task family)

When a grid contains repeated horizontal motifs of the form `A, B, A, B, A...` against a separate background, convert the *intervening B cells* between adjacent A cells in those horizontal alternating runs to color `2`. Preserve all A cells, all other cells, and the original grid dimensions. Do not fill vertical gaps or gaps next to a run endpoint. If a row has `A B A`, output `A 2 A`; if `A B A B A`, output `A 2 A 2 A`. Apply to each horizontal run, regardless of where in the grid it occurs. The examples used different palette pairs, but inserted color was consistently 2.

Observed demo palette cases: foreground 1 over background 3; foreground 6 over background 9. In the solved test, foreground was 9 over background 6; only the 6s directly between adjacent 9s in horizontal alternating runs became 2. Rows/cells outside such gaps remain unchanged.

Careful: output must keep every row's original width and the grid's original height. Before submission, verify row lengths and change only the gap cells. The task evaluation gives only correct/incorrect feedback; one demo was enough to infer this rule, though demos cost an attempt."
